 (Q^a f)_ij=J sum_z P^a_iz(f_zj-f_ij)
                    +J sum_z P^a_jz(f_iz-f_ij),
 b^a_ij=J(P^a_ij+P^a_ji)=-Q^a1=-(Q^a)^*1.

Let

 eta=2J/sqrt(n-1),    rho=2eta/gamma,
 alpha=gamma-rho eta,
 K_n=n/(n-1)(2J+8J^2/gamma),
 Psi=2(n-1)eta/(n alpha),
 e=1/2+[n/(2(n-1))]rho,    Rnorm=sqrt(1+rho^2).

Assume n-1>=4J/gamma+16(J/gamma)^2, so alpha>=gamma/2. In each region
retain the causal public response

  (r^a)'=n c_a[Q^a r^a+<b^a,r^a>r^a],
  kappa_a=n<b^a,r^a>,
  a_a(t)=c_a(t)kappa_a(t).                             (2.1)

Its initial value is nonnegative, symmetric, mean one, and lies in the tube
||r^a-1||<=rho. Canonical r^a=1 is always allowed. The same tube is invariant
for every deterministic profile and every admitted restart. In particular

           0<=a_a(t)<=A:=cbar K_n.                     (2.2)

The target is the k-coordinate stochastic physical field

  dX_a=(M_t X)_a dt+sqrt[a_a(t)(1-X_a^2)]dB_a,
                 a=1,...,k,                           (2.3)

with independent coordinate Brownian motions. Migration is inward on every
boundary face of [-1,1]^k. For finite k, coordinatewise square-root uniqueness
and Lipschitz migration give a positive well-posed SDE; the constants for
this existence statement need not be used in the comparison estimates.
Coefficients a_a are public history functions, not hidden-state functions.

The initial JOINT law of (X_1,...,X_k) is exactly the pushforward of the
microscopic initial law under its regional means, conditional on declared
public data/coins. Any arrangement or correlation of microscopic spins is
allowed. This requirement can be costly for an arbitrary prior; that cost
is not removed by the theorem. No independence between regions is assumed.

3. WHY ONLY INTERNAL MIXING IS NEEDED

For each donor region b set beta_i^{ab}=sum_j C^{ab}_ij sigma_j^b. Direct
calculation and double stochasticity give

  L x_a=sum_(b!=a)nu_ab(x_b-x_a)=(Mx)_a,
  Gamma(x_a,x_b)=0 for a!=b.                           (3.1)

Within a region use D^a_ij=(1-sigma_i^a sigma_j^a)/2,
h_a=<1,D^a>=[n/(n-1)](1-x_a^2)/2, and E_a=D^a-h_a r^a.
For a cross-copy input from b the exact pair forcing is

 B^{ab}_ij=1-(sigma_j^a beta_i^{ab}+sigma_i^a beta_j^{ab})/2
                         -2D^a_ij,   |B^{ab}_ij|<=2.

Thus the unprojected hidden pair force sum_b nu_ab B^{ab} has norm at most
2Lambda. After subtracting its response projection, the force in E_a has
norm at most 2Lambda(1+Rnorm). It enters the residual equation

 dE_a=n c_a[Q^a E_a+r^a<b^a,E_a>]dt
        +sum_b nu_ab[B^{ab}-r^a<1,B^{ab}>]dt+dM^{E_a}. (3.2)

The unknown donor spin means have not been declared controls or factorized.
An event whose recipient is in another region leaves E_a and its corrector
unchanged, even if that event uses a donor from region a.

The coordinate bracket decomposes exactly as

 Gamma(x_a)=a_a(1-x_a^2)+R_a+e_a,
 R_a=2(n-1)c_a<b^a,E_a>,
 0<=e_a=Gamma_cross(x_a)<=4Lambda/n.                    (3.3)

Uniform coordinate bounds are

  Gamma(x_a)<=G:=4J cbar+4Lambda/n,
  |Delta x_a|<=2/n.                                   (3.4)

For every deterministic complete public profile on an interval of length T,
the previous internal dual construction gives terminal-zero functions V_a
with

  (partial_t+L_micro)V_a=-R_a+F_a,
  |V_a|<=v:=Psi e,
  |F_a|<=f:=2Lambda Psi(1+Rnorm),
  sum_events rate |Delta x_a Delta V_a|
       <=q_*:=4(J cbar+Lambda/n)Psi(1+rho).             (3.5)

Only recipient events in region a contribute to the last sum. These are
uniform bounds in k. They use the internal coercive gap, not the gap of the
coarse migration matrix. The functions V_a are deterministic-profile proof
correctors; they are not additional adapted physical memory under feedback.

4. THE OBSERVABLE ALGEBRA AND A FINITE-LINEAGE REPRESENTATION

Let A_D(k) be polynomials in the allele variables p_a=(x_a+1)/2 of total
degree at most D. In the usual monomial basis set

  f=sum_beta f_beta p^beta,
  ||f||_alg=sum_beta |f_beta|.                          (4.1)

This norm dominates the sup norm on [0,1]^k, has unit norm for the constant
one, and is submultiplicative. Multiplication adds total degree.

For the target field, in allele coordinates its generator satisfies

 L_t p^beta
  =sum_(a!=b) beta_a nu_ab
               [p^(beta-e_a+e_b)-p^beta]
     +(1/2)sum_a a_a beta_a(beta_a-1)
               [p^(beta-e_a)-p^beta].                 (4.2)

This is the generator of a positive conservative chain on multiindices of
degree at most D: a lineage migrates with the ORIGINAL row rates nu_ab, and
two lineages in one region merge at the displayed pair rate. Total degree
does not increase. Its total rate is at most

               D Lambda+(A/2)D(D-1),                 (4.3)

independent of k. For backward physical evolution, this finite-degree
coefficient chain reads the public commands in reverse chronological order.
It is not an adjoint migration kernel in the regional counting measure.

Consequently the target backward semigroup preserves A_D and contracts
coefficient norm, for arbitrary time-dependent commands. If g(s,x) is the
target backward expectation of f, then

                 ||g(s,.)||_alg<=||f||_alg.            (4.4)

This follows directly from positivity and conservation of the coefficient
chain, or from its finite-dimensional time-dependent matrix equation. It
does not require coarse migration column balance, a stationary environment,
or an equilibrium initial spin law.

For every FIXED time s, coefficient contraction also gives the aggregate
derivative estimate

 S_r(g(s)):=sum_(i_1,...,i_r)
        ||partial_(i_1)...partial_(i_r)g(s,.)||_infinity
        <=||f||_alg T_r(D),
 T_r(D)=(D)_r/2^r,  with T_r=0 when D<r.              (4.5)

Indeed the sum of the absolute derivative maxima of one p-monomial of degree
d is exactly (d)_r/2^r: each x derivative contributes one half, and the
ordered derivative selections count d(d-1)...(d-r+1). Sum the absolute
coefficients and use d<=D. All maxima are only over spatial states here.

The ordering of bounds matters: (4.5) holds after summing derivative norms
at EACH TIME, and is then integrated in time. It does not assert a bound
on sum_indices sup_{s,x}|partial^r g|. Migration can move coefficient mass
between regions at different times. That stronger time-supremum assertion
is unnecessary and has not been used.

5. DIMENSION-INDEPENDENT MICROSCOPIC POLYNOMIAL CERTIFICATE

Put

 C_D=(2Lambda+A)T_2+2A T_3+(A+G)T_4/2,

 E_D(n,T)
  =(1/2){vT_2+T[fT_2+vC_D+q_*T_3]}
       +(T/n)[2Lambda T_2+(G/3)T_3].                  (5.1)

Then, for every finite k, every deterministic admitted public profile,
every initial microscopic state and every response restart in its tube,

 |E_sigma f(p(t))-(Q_target(0,t)f)(p(sigma))|
                       <=||f||_alg E_D(n,t)            (5.2)

for f in A_D. For fixed D,t,J,gamma,cbar,Lambda this tends to zero as
n->infinity, with a bound independent of k. Constants can be replaced by
their nondecreasing envelopes in D if desired.

Proof. Work with the target backward polynomial g, normalized to coefficient
norm at most one. Its microscopic generator discrepancy is

        (1/2)sum_a (R_a+e_a) g_aa + cubic remainder.

The cubic remainder summed over all regions is at most GT_3/(3n), using
the coordinate jump bound 2/n and the aggregate derivative bound. It is not
bounded by first taking an individual derivative maximum and multiplying
by the number of regions.

For w_a=g_aa, differentiation of the backward equation gives

 partial_t w_a
  =-sum_i (Mx)_i partial_i w_a
       -2sum_i M_ia g_ia
       +a_a w_a+2a_a x_a g_aaa
       -(1/2)sum_i a_i(1-x_i^2)g_iiaa.                (5.3)

The exact microscopic drift cancels the first term. Expand the microscopic
jump action on w_a only to first order. At a fixed time, summing its spatial
supremum over a gives at most C_D: use |M_ia|<=Lambda, (4.5), and the two
second-order sums bounded by (A+G)T_4/2. No column-sum bound on M is needed.

Apply the jump product identity to each w_a V_a, using V_a(T)=0. Sum over a
BEFORE integrating the spatial derivative bounds. Equations (3.5) and (4.5)
give

 |E integral sum_a R_a g_aa|
       <=vT_2+T[fT_2+vC_D+q_*T_3].                    (5.4)

The factor one half in the generator gives the first line of (5.1). The
direct cross bracket costs 2Lambda T T_2/n, and the cubic remainder costs
GT T_3/(3n), proving the second line. Dynkin's identity proves (5.2).
For arbitrary initial priors, integrate its all-state bound.

As a consistency check, E_D=0 for D=0,1: constants and first moments satisfy
the exact common drift law. Higher-degree tests detect the unresolved
fluctuation law and require the pair-response correction.

6. A GENERAL OBSERVABLE-ALGEBRA PRINCIPLE FOR CONTROLLED RECORDS

The passage from (5.2) to complete-record accuracy is not specific to spin
monomials. Here is the general classical interface being used.

Let A_0 subset A_1 subset ... be a filtered commutative algebra of functions
on a target hidden state space, with 1 in A_0, ||1||_alg=1, sup norm bounded
by algebra norm, multiplication of degree r and s going to degree r+s,
and submultiplicative norm. Suppose EVERY admitted deterministic-profile
target transition preserves degrees and contracts this norm. Suppose the
microscopic endpoint estimate at every hidden state/public restart is

 |E_micro f(projected state at t+h)-Q_target f(current projection)|
                    <=||f||_alg E_D(n,h), f in A_D,    (6.1)

where E_D(n,h)->0 at fixed D,h. The initial target law is the exact projected
joint law. Let a fixed real observable phi in A_1 satisfy

                    |phi|<=1,  ||phi||_alg<=B, B>=1.  (6.2)

Use the same bounded-energy Gaussian observation policy

 dY_t=H_t phi(state_t)dt+dW_t,
              integral_0^T |H_t|^2dt<=Gamma.           (6.3)

Assume the canonical causal reference construction and the physical scalar
modulus bounds stated below. Then (6.1), including its uniform restart and
public-context qualifications, is sufficient for complete-record TV
convergence. It does not require a metric approximation of the whole hidden
state or a finite-dimensional posterior filter.

Why products across time are controlled. For times t_i and a simple temporal
product prod_i f_i(state(t_i)), recursively propagate the future product
backwards using the target semigroups. Its degree is at most the sum of
the factor degrees, and its algebra norm is at most the product of future
factor norms. The microscopic conditional telescope uses the actual full
hidden state at each restart. Past factors have sup norms bounded by their
algebra norms. Hence each step error is at most E_D times the product of all
factor norms. Summing over steps and extending linearly gives q E_D times
the degree-D finite projective tensor norm of a q-time test. This norm is
the infimum of sums of products of factor norms over finite tensor
representations for which the SUM of factor degrees in each term is at most
D. Equivalently, the proof may charge any displayed representation satisfying
that degree constraint. Tensor multiplication is submultiplicative with
its degrees added.

This algebra criterion is sufficient; it is not a necessary characterization
of all useful effective laws. It identifies an actual stable prediction
interface. A family of static state reconstructions alone would not supply
the common semigroup and restart properties required in (6.1).

7. EXPLICIT GAUSSIAN-RECORD BOUND, INDEPENDENT OF FIELD SIZE

For the regional application choose FIXED deterministic spatial weights
w_a with sum_a|w_a|<=1, and observe phi(x)=sum_a w_a x_a. This includes a
single local regional probe. The weights may differ with n and k, but are
fixed during each experiment. In allele variables ||phi||_alg<=3, so B=3.

Since |(Mx)_a|<=2Lambda and at most one coordinate jumps,

 |drift(phi(x))|<=2Lambda,
 Gamma_micro(phi)<=G sum_a w_a^2<=G,
 |Delta phi(x)|<=2/n,
 Gamma_target(phi)<=A sum_a w_a^2<=A.                  (7.1)

All bounds hold on the original physical laws under the common policy.
They remain independent of k even for a local probe with w concentrated
at one region. There is no reliance on a global average becoming noiseless.

Let q>=1, h=T/q, R>0, L>=1, and Gamma>0. Define

 M_obs=R+Gamma/2,
 r_L(M_obs)=exp(M_obs) M_obs^(L+1)/(L+1)!,
 p_bad=min{1,q Gamma/R^2,2^q exp[-R^2/(2Gamma)]},

 F_freeze(n,q)=sqrt(Gamma){2Lambda h
      +[G^2 T h+4GT/n^2]^(1/4)+[A^2 T h]^(1/4)}.

Then the physical record laws, including declared controller coins, obey

 TV(P_micro^(coins,Y),P_field^(coins,Y))
 <=min{1, F_freeze(n,q)+r_L(M_obs)
     +(q/2)exp(3R+9Gamma/2)E_(2L)(n,h)
     +exp(Gamma/2)sqrt(p_bad)}.                       (7.2)

For Gamma=0 the output is the common reference Wiener record, giving zero
error directly. The infimum over proof parameters in (7.2) is permitted.
They are proof approximation parameters, not changes to the actual policy.

Derivation. On the reference record, freeze ONLY the hidden observed scalar
at times t_i=ih, without freezing any controls or H. Set

 A_i=integral_(t_i)^(t_(i+1)) H_t dot dY_t,
 B_i=integral_(t_i)^(t_(i+1)) |H_t|^2dt,
 S=sum_i|A_i|.

The frozen likelihood is exp(Q), where

 Q=sum_i A_i phi_i-(1/2)sum_i B_i phi_i^2.              (7.3)

Conditional on the COMPLETE reference record and public coins, all profiles,
responses, A_i and B_i are deterministic. This is an ordinary function of
the hidden skeleton. On S<=R, |Q|<=M_obs. Truncate exp(Q) at Taylor order L.
It has total observable degree <=2L, uniform scalar remainder at most r_L,
and temporal projective norm at most exp(BR+B^2 Gamma/2). For B=3 this is
the coefficient in (7.2). The multitime algebra telescope bounds the two
conditional expectations by q times this norm times E_(2L). Charge the
Taylor remainder under both hidden laws and the one-half factor of TV.

For the bad event, Ito isometry gives E_reference S^2<=q Gamma. Alternatively,
S is the maximum over 2^q signed stochastic integrals, each with quadratic
variation at most Gamma; the exponential martingale bound gives the second
tail allowance in p_bad. These do not require independent increments of A_i.
Each true or frozen bounded-energy likelihood has second moment at most
exp(Gamma). Cauchy--Schwarz therefore gives exactly the final term of (7.2).

Finally, unfreeze on EACH original causal physical space. Relative entropy
between a model's true and frozen observation likelihoods is

  (1/2) E_true integral |H_t|^2|Z_t-Z_(floor(t/h)h)|^2dt.

Pinsker gives sqrt(Gamma) times the scalar L2 modulus divided by two.
A signal with drift bound a0, bracket rate G0 and jumps bounded by b0 obeys

 omega<=a0 h+2(G0^2 T h+b0^2 G0 T)^(1/4).

Use (a0,G0,b0)=(2Lambda,G,2/n) and (2Lambda,A,0) and sum the two unfreezing
errors. This gives F_freeze. No stochastic calculation takes place under a
future-conditioned hidden coupling; in fact this proof needs no such coupling.

For fixed physical budgets, first choose finite q, then R, then L, and
finally take n large. Every choice and every allowance is independent of k.
Thus (7.2) tends to zero uniformly even along arbitrary finite k=k_n. The
explicit constants are conservative and may require very large n; no useful
finite-size performance threshold or numerical simulation gain is inferred.

8. WHAT THE RESULT CLOSES, AND WHAT IT RETAINS

The construction retains a spatial field of slow physical variables X_a.
It need not compress that field into one scalar. The two-region preparation
counterexample already proves that total mean plus control history can miss
macroscopic physical information. The present theorem allows arbitrarily
many such fields without a dimension factor in the specified record error.

Inside each region, the public pair response retains the causal response
of eliminated fast internal degrees of freedom. If the internal control
family has a bounded common equitable pair quotient and the initial response
belongs to it, the field has finitely many response coordinates per region.
Complete internal averaging has kappa_a=2J exactly, leaving the standard
interacting Wright--Fisher field with public activity coefficients.

For a generic internally mixing graph, a response array can still contain
order n^2 numbers per region. The recent local-return representation can
replace it with a certified history functional. For canonical response
initialization and the stronger held size condition it supplies

 |kappa_a-g_a|<=delta_(n,Lhist)
     =C_n exp(-beta_n Lhist)+K_n^2 Lhist/n,

uniformly in the region, profile and time, with C_n and beta_n from the held
history theorem. If this bound is uniform over all regions and histories,
replacing every kappa_a by g_a adds only

       (cbar T delta_(n,Lhist)/2) T_2(D)               (8.1)

to E_D(n,T). The proof uses the ORIGINAL response/corrector and charges the
coefficient discrepancy in the target generator via the aggregate derivative
sum. There is no multiplicative factor k. Positive bounded public replacement
coefficients preserve the observable algebra and all likelihood arguments.

Thus the local-return history reduction and the many-region field theorem
compose at their actual interface. A window Lhist->infinity with Lhist/n->0
preserves convergence. Evaluation costs and public prehistory at restarts
must still be retained. A history functional is not a finite recursive law.

The finite-lineage formula (4.2) is also a useful representation of finite
polynomial predictions: at most D ancestral lines are needed at degree D,
with proposal envelope (4.3). This does not make required graph rows,
time-dependent response coefficients, initial joint moments, or precision
free. The theorem is not an efficient whole-record sampling algorithm.

9. FAILED STRONGER NORM AND THE NEXT SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY

A tempting route was to approximate every Lipschitz function of the full
regional state by tensor Bernstein polynomials and bound all tested fourth
derivatives independently of k. The separate adversarial calculation finds
that this route fails: even fixed Bernstein degree two can have a fourth-
derivative aggregate growing as sqrt(k) for a function with unit Lipschitz
constant in the averaged l1 metric. Boundary variance weights do not remove
that example. This is failure of that pointwise norm estimate, not a proof
that the physical field limit or all metric approaches fail.

The observable-algebra route succeeds because it uses a different question:
which finite-degree functions are generated by a fixed bounded observation
experiment and its backward dynamics? It does not assume a dimension-free
coefficient bound for arbitrary full-state Lipschitz tests.

The fixed spatial observation is a real restriction. If the sensor may sweep
through an unbounded bank of regional coordinates within a proof interval,
the reference stochastic integral produces a vector of spatial coefficients.
Its l1 norm can grow with the number of visited regions even with fixed
observation energy. The present scalar cutoff argument does not control that
larger class uniformly. This is a missing observation-interface estimate,
not a demonstrated impossibility of moving-sensor prediction.

Other open interfaces include nonlinear constitutive laws without a stable
observable algebra, imperfect or nonuniform internal mixing, unbalanced
microscopic donor kernels, quantum measurement backaction, and continuum
spatial limits. None is inferred merely from the existing static Astra
reconstruction statements. The present result isolates one constructive
mechanism and its operational scope.

10. PROOF SOURCES AND EVIDENCE

The exact internal coercivity, tube, and terminal-dual inputs are preserved in
 CAUSAL_PAIR_RESPONSE_ON_CONTROLLED_MIXING_GRAPHS.txt
 SHA256 d4620ddc9167cfbc2878eb7cc8a8f035595655e64b8fc425472c460a020586f7.

The fully scoped two-region source is preserved separately as
 SLOW_REGIONAL_FIELDS_AND_CAUSAL_FAST_RESPONSES_V2.txt
 SHA256 c98b0abce63403cb8a3d2b900055ba837e2198760f48bf32917b2a5d3a371a06.

The local-return physical coefficient theorem is
 CAUSAL_LOCAL_PAIR_RETURN_REPRESENTATION_V2.txt
 SHA256 c140df219bcbfe4947a45b810f29a9562008de842a96cb0db9102aa421ce3adc.

The new many-region microscopic polynomial and complete-record/algebra
interfaces are being frozen as separate independent producer sources by
the existing warm workers. Their exact final pins and integration checks
belong in a separate audit, without rewriting these proofs. The separate
failed-norm construction is retained as a genuine change of representation.

All displayed constructions are mathematical proofs or explicitly stated
conditional interfaces. No acquired physical measurement, new public
disclosure, finite-size technological advantage, or established novelty is
claimed. Existing primary coalescent, polynomial-process, effective-memory,
and interacting-diffusion approaches are compatible predecessors.

OBSERVABLE ALGEBRAS AND EFFECTIVE LAWS FOR ARBITRARILY MANY SLOW REGIONS

Private ASTRA-FRESH-20261023 / P1. 23 October 2026 UTC.
This is new mathematical work. All earlier sources are preserved.

0. THE CONCRETE RESULT AND THE CHANGE OF REPRESENTATION

There is no need to keep the number of slow physical regions fixed in the
regional closure theorem. For any finite number k=k_n of regions, each of n
microscopic spins, the construction below approximates the COMPLETE noisy
record of a fixed bounded linear spatial probe by an interacting diffusion
field. The error bound is independent of k. Thus k_n may grow arbitrarily
with n. There is no global mixing-gap condition and no balance condition on
the directed coarse migration graph. Fast mixing is required only INSIDE
each region; each microscopic cross-region donor kernel remains balanced.

All internal graphs, internal activities, migration rates and cross kernels
may use the same actual observation-feedback algorithm. Their bounds and the
observation time/energy budget are fixed. The observation's spatial weights
are fixed during an experiment. Initial regional JOINT state information is
supplied, not reconstructed from the observed scalar.

The key representation is a filtered algebra of observable tests. Its norm
counts polynomial coefficient mass, rather than the dimension of the hidden
physical field. The target dynamics preserve this algebra and contract its
norm. Small microscopic errors on each finite-degree sector then control
every event in the complete noisy record, via a finite Taylor approximation
of the observation likelihood. No full-field Wasserstein coupling is used.

This is a scoped mathematical capability: observation-law prediction remains
controlled as the number of slow regions increases. It is not a claim of an
economical solver for all coefficients, a finite observer posterior, a novel
interacting Wright--Fisher process, or a theory of arbitrary physical matter.
Polynomial duality, stochastic averaging, and projection memory have strong
established predecessors. Novelty of the precise controlled combination and
practical advantage remain UNKNOWN.

1. MICROSCOPIC FIELD, CONTROLS, AND PHYSICAL SCALING

There are k regions, each containing n>=3 spins sigma_i^a in {-1,+1}.
The number k is finite for every model but is not bounded in the theorem.
Write

  x_a=n^{-1}sum_i sigma_i^a,      p_a=(x_a+1)/2.

Let J>0, gamma>0, cbar<infinity and Lambda<infinity be fixed. In region a,
each site copies an internal donor at rate nJ c_a(t), using a doubly
stochastic kernel P^a_t, where 0<=c_a<=cbar. Every admitted internal kernel
satisfies the common additive-reversibilization Poincare inequality

 <f,J[I-(P^a+(P^a)^T)/2]f>_n
       >=gamma(||f||_n^2-<1,f>_n^2).                   (1.1)

For a!=b, a receiving site in region a copies a donor in region b at rate
nu_ab(t), using an arbitrary doubly stochastic n by n kernel C^{ab}_t.
Assume

  nu_ab>=0,    lambda_a:=sum_(b!=a)nu_ab<=Lambda.       (1.2)

Define M_ab=nu_ab for a!=b and M_aa=-lambda_a. It is a row-conservative
coarse migration generator. Its columns need not sum to zero. Consequently
the full microscopic network need not be globally balanced, and the global
mean need not be a martingale. Recipient sites alone change in each event.

The physical clock here accelerates INTERNAL per-site rate J by n. It does
not accelerate by the total number kn. On an unaccelerated internal rate-J
clock, a fixed horizon T here costs time nT and migration rates scale as 1/n.
This convention retains order-one regional fluctuations and order-one slow
exchange, regardless of the number of regions. It is part of the model.

The public commands may be bounded measurable predictable functions of a
canonical noisy record and declared independent controller coins. They have
no access to hidden spins, hidden field values, or primitive hidden noises.
All comparison experiments use the SAME actual policy. Finite-state chains
are nonexplosive for finite k,n. Causal well-posed reference constructions
and measurable profile-dependent transition kernels are assumed as in the
previous controlled-response theorem.

2. INTERNAL RESPONSE AND THE PHYSICAL TARGET FIELD

On ordered unequal pairs within region a, with normalized uniform inner
product and zero diagonal, define

 (Q^a f)_ij=J sum_z P^a_iz(f_zj-f_ij)
                    +J sum_z P^a_jz(f_iz-f_ij),
 b^a_ij=J(P^a_ij+P^a_ji)=-Q^a1=-(Q^a)^*1.

Let

 eta=2J/sqrt(n-1),    rho=2eta/gamma,
 alpha=gamma-rho eta,
 K_n=n/(n-1)(2J+8J^2/gamma),
 Psi=2(n-1)eta/(n alpha),
 e=1/2+[n/(2(n-1))]rho,    Rnorm=sqrt(1+rho^2).

Assume n-1>=4J/gamma+16(J/gamma)^2, so alpha>=gamma/2. In each region
retain the causal public response

  (r^a)'=n c_a[Q^a r^a+<b^a,r^a>r^a],
  kappa_a=n<b^a,r^a>,
  a_a(t)=c_a(t)kappa_a(t).                             (2.1)

Its initial value is nonnegative, symmetric, mean one, and lies in the tube
||r^a-1||<=rho. Canonical r^a=1 is always allowed. The same tube is invariant
for every deterministic profile and every admitted restart. In particular

           0<=a_a(t)<=A:=cbar K_n.                     (2.2)

The target is the k-coordinate stochastic physical field

  dX_a=(M_t X)_a dt+sqrt[a_a(t)(1-X_a^2)]dB_a,
                 a=1,...,k,                           (2.3)

with independent coordinate Brownian motions. Migration is inward on every
boundary face of [-1,1]^k. For finite k, coordinatewise square-root uniqueness

9. FAILED STRONGER NORM AND THE NEXT SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY

A tempting route was to approximate every Lipschitz function of the full
regional state by tensor Bernstein polynomials and bound all tested fourth
derivatives independently of k. The separate adversarial calculation finds
that this route fails: even fixed Bernstein degree two can have a fourth-
derivative aggregate growing as sqrt(k) for a function with unit Lipschitz
constant in the averaged l1 metric. Boundary variance weights do not remove
that example. This is failure of that pointwise norm estimate, not a proof
that the physical field limit or all metric approaches fail.

The observable-algebra route succeeds because it uses a different question:
which finite-degree functions are generated by a fixed bounded observation
experiment and its backward dynamics? It does not assume a dimension-free
coefficient bound for arbitrary full-state Lipschitz tests.

The fixed spatial observation is a real restriction. If the sensor may sweep
through an unbounded bank of regional coordinates within a proof interval,
the reference stochastic integral produces a vector of spatial coefficients.
Its l1 norm can grow with the number of visited regions even with fixed
observation energy. The present scalar cutoff argument does not control that
larger class uniformly. This is a missing observation-interface estimate,
not a demonstrated impossibility of moving-sensor prediction.

Other open interfaces include nonlinear constitutive laws without a stable
observable algebra, imperfect or nonuniform internal mixing, unbalanced
microscopic donor kernels, quantum measurement backaction, and continuum
spatial limits. None is inferred merely from the existing static Astra
reconstruction statements. The present result isolates one constructive
mechanism and its operational scope.
